canonical.title: React i18n 2026: the translation pipeline, not just the library

parent.title: Decision framework: which React i18n library to adopt in 2026

siblings.title: React i18n in 2026: The Core Library Head-to-Head
siblings.summary: react-i18next is still the safe default; next-intl owns the Next.js App Router; Paraglide and Lingui are the compile-time challengers worth betting on.

siblings.title: Message format, pluralization & ICU across React i18n libraries (2026)
siblings.summary: ICU-first (react-intl, next-intl, Lingui) vs interpolation-first (i18next default, typesafe-i18n) vs MF2-inspired (Paraglide) — how each authors plurals, gender and Intl-formatted numbers/dates.

siblings.title: Type safety, extraction & developer tooling for React i18n in 2026
siblings.summary: Compile-first libraries (Paraglide, typesafe-i18n) and next-intl give type safety for free; i18next and react-intl bolt it on via declaration files and CLI extraction.

siblings.title: React i18n in 2026: framework & runtime fit (React 19, RSC, Vite vs Next.js)
siblings.summary: next-intl or Lingui for the Next.js App Router; Paraglide or react-i18next for a Vite SPA — the split is compile-time (tree-shakeable) vs runtime-dictionary architecture.

sources.title: i18next — Translation Management Systems
sources.claim: Locize is the official i18next TMS with a runtime backend and native CLI commands; 11 other TMSes integrate but with less depth.

sources.title: locize — i18next-cli instrument
sources.claim: A June 2026 i18next-cli command chains instrument, extract, Locize setup, and AI auto-translation in one run.

sources.title: Tolgee — React i18n libraries comparison
sources.claim: react-intl's extract-and-compile pipeline is powerful but fiddly; Lingui extract pulls messages into a PO catalog; Tolgee SDK wraps rendered strings for Alt-click editing.

sources.title: Lingui — Message extraction
sources.claim: lingui extract analyzes source code and extracts all messages into per-locale catalogs, merging with existing translations so they survive.

sources.title: Lingui — Catalog formats
sources.claim: Lingui supports PO (default), JSON, and CSV; PO supports translator comments, metadata, and contexts.

sources.title: Crowdin — Lingui i18n
sources.claim: Lingui CLI extracts messages into gettext PO files translated via Crowdin and compiled into optimized JSON/JS catalogs, with automated CI/CD sync.

sources.title: Crowdin Store — Lingui String Exporter
sources.claim: Crowdin ships a Lingui String Exporter app to handle Lingui PO catalogs on the platform.

sources.title: inlang — Tools
sources.claim: inlang ecosystem tools: Paraglide, inlang CLI, Sherlock VS Code extension, Fink CAT editor, and a macOS i18n editor.

sources.title: Paraglide JS (opral/paraglide-js)
sources.claim: Paraglide JS is a compiler-based i18n library emitting tree-shakable translations for up to 70% smaller bundles.

sources.title: inlang — Fink Localization Editor
sources.claim: Fink lets translators edit messages in a git repo via a web app without cloning the repo or using the git CLI.

sources.title: next-intl — Localization management
sources.claim: next-intl uses JSON message files and recommends Crowdin, integrating via CLI, GitHub app, webhooks, OTA SDK, or manual up/download.

sources.title: next-intl — Extraction (useExtracted)
sources.claim: next-intl's experimental useExtracted hook auto-extracts messages with no key naming and no CLI, via a Turbopack/Webpack loader.

sources.title: next-intl — useExtracted announcement
sources.claim: useExtracted makes labels eligible for translation with no key naming and no CLI; experimental in next-intl@4.5, needs Next.js 16+.

sources.title: typesafe-i18n (codingcommons/typesafe-i18n)
sources.claim: typesafe-i18n is a fully type-safe zero-dependency i18n library with dev-mode codegen and no built-in TMS.

sources.title: FormatJS — Message extraction
sources.claim: FormatJS CLI extracts message IDs into JSON; a babel plugin/AST transformer auto-inserts IDs.

sources.title: FormatJS — CLI
sources.claim: @formatjs/cli ships built-in formatters for crowdin, lokalise, smartling, transifex, plus custom formatters.

sources.title: Tolgee — In-context translating
sources.claim: Tolgee in-context editing works via Alt+click on any text in the running app, functions even in production, with one-click screenshot capture.

sources.title: Tolgee — AI translation
sources.claim: Tolgee integrates DeepL, Google Translate, and AWS Translate out of the box with app-extracted context.

sources.title: i18n-keyless — Best i18next alternatives 2026
sources.claim: By mid-2026 official MCP servers ship for Locize, Crowdin, Lokalise, Phrase, POEditor, Tolgee, and SimpleLocalize; BYOK LLM keys supported.

sources.title: Lokalise — MCP for localization
sources.claim: MCP lets AI agents add keys, create tasks, and check progress in a TMS without API scripts or switching UIs.

sources.title: inlang — Ninja i18n GitHub Lint Action
sources.claim: Ninja i18n is a GitHub lint action that automates i18n linting for pull requests.

sources.title: i18n-check (lingualdev/i18n-check)
sources.claim: i18n-check validates ICU and i18next translation files, finding missing and broken translations in CI.

sources.title: Autonoma — Catching missing translations
sources.claim: A build-time lint step comparing key sets across locale files is the cheap first CI gate, running in under a second.

sources.title: Localhero — Automate i18n with GitHub Actions
sources.claim: Teams automate i18n via GitHub Actions using three approaches including missing-translation health checks.

sources.title: Weblate — Features
sources.claim: Weblate is a self-hostable continuous localization platform with tight git integration used by 2500+ libre projects, supports React Intl JSON.

sources.title: Weblate (WeblateOrg/weblate)
sources.claim: Weblate is a web-based localization tool with tight version control integration.

sources.title: Tolgee vs Crowdin
sources.claim: Tolgee is an open-source, self-hostable Lokalise/Crowdin alternative with native React SDK and in-context editing.

sources.title: locize — i18next and inlang interop
sources.claim: i18next and inlang can interoperate, letting teams keep i18next runtime while using inlang tooling.

sources.title: Phrase — React i18n with FormatJS
sources.claim: react-intl/FormatJS integrates with TMS platforms like Phrase Strings for the extract-translate-import cycle.

sources.title: FormatJS — react-intl
sources.claim: react-intl formats strings/numbers/dates/plurals using ICU MessageFormat natively.
